correctness.rationale: Over GF(2), removing the hub leaves disjoint paths; their endpoint-neighborhood vectors belong to each path adjacency-image, proving rank 2s by alternating congruence. The Eulerian all-ones kernel vector implies each side of a rank-tight biclique cover has even size, excluding equality if edge count is odd. Explicit two-biclique paired triangles, two-biclique singleton triangle, one-biclique squares, and a K2,2 edge-subdivision identity construct matching covers for all lengths. All assumptions and both parity boundaries are covered, and independent finite checker tests 1,484 witnesses/ranks plus ten small optima.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general rank inequality, even-core obstruction, and exact disjoint-union results are not strong enough to determine an arbitrary vertex-identified bouquet. Theorem 8 applies to disjoint unions, not coalescences; known bipartite equality handles only bouquets with exclusively even petals.
